proof.limit-comparison-test.stewart.notes: Since aₙ/bₙ → c > 0, for large n we have (c/2)bₙ ≤ aₙ ≤ 2c·bₙ. The result follows from the Comparison Test applied in both directions.

sources.author: James Stewart

proof.limit-cosx-minus-1-over-x.stewart.notes: Multiply numerator and denominator by (cos x + 1), use the identity cos²x - 1 = -sin²x, then apply the limit laws and the result lim sin(x)/x = 1.

proof.limit-exists-iff-one-sided-limits..notes: Follows from the epsilon-delta definitions: if both one-sided limits equal L, then for any epsilon the appropriate delta works for x on either side of a.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.limit-laws.stewart.notes: Stewart proves the sum law (law 1) in detail using the epsilon-delta definition in Appendix F. The other laws are proved similarly. The product law requires the triangle inequality and boundedness of one factor near the limit point.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.limit-one-over-x-at-infinity.stewa.notes: For any epsilon > 0, take N = (1/epsilon)^(1/r). Then x > N implies 1/x^r < epsilon.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.limit-power-law.stewart.notes: Follows by repeated application of the product law (law 4) with g = f, using induction on n.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.limit-root-law.stewart.notes: Stewart states this law without a full proof in section 2.3. A rigorous proof requires continuity of the nth root function, which depends on the completeness of the real numbers.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.limit-sinx-over-x.stewart.notes: Stewart uses a geometric argument comparing areas in the unit circle: area of triangle <= area of sector <= area of outer triangle, yielding cos(x) <= sin(x)/x <= 1 for 0 < x < pi/2. The squeeze theorem then gives the result.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.local-extremum-at-critical.stewart.notes: If f has a local extremum at c, then either f'(c) does not exist (so c is critical by definition) or f'(c) exists and equals 0 by Fermat's theorem (so c is also critical).

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.mean-value-theorem-integrals.stewa.notes: Since f is continuous on [a, b], by the Extreme Value Theorem it attains its absolute minimum m and maximum M. By the integral comparison property, m(b-a) ≤ ∫_a^b f(x) dx ≤ M(b-a), so m ≤ (1/(b-a))∫_a^b f(x) dx ≤ M. Since f is continuous and f_avg lies between m and M, the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees a number c in [a, b] with f(c) = f_avg.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.mean-value-theorem.stewart.notes: Define h(x) = f(x) - [f(a) + ((f(b)-f(a))/(b-a))(x - a)]. Then h is continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b), and h(a) = h(b) = 0. By Rolle's theorem, there exists c in (a,b) with h'(c) = 0, which gives f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a).

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.monotonic-sequence-theorem.stewart.notes: Stewart states this theorem relies on the Completeness Axiom (every nonempty bounded above set of reals has a least upper bound). He does not provide a formal proof. The argument is: if {aₙ} is increasing and bounded above, let L = sup{aₙ}. Then for any ε > 0, L - ε is not an upper bound, so there exists N with aₙ > L - ε for n > N. Since aₙ ≤ L, we have |aₙ - L| < ε.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.net-change-theorem.stewart.notes: Direct application of FTC Part 2 with f = F'.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.power-rule-combined-chain.stewart.notes: Let y = u^n where u = g(x). By the chain rule, dy/dx = (dy/du)(du/dx) = nu^{n-1} · g'(x).

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.power-rule.stewart.notes: For positive integer n, expand (x+h)^n using the Binomial Theorem: (x+h)^n = x^n + nx^{n-1}h + terms with h^2 or higher. Then f'(x) = lim(h→0) [(x+h)^n - x^n]/h = nx^{n-1}. The general case (all real n) is deferred to section 3.6 via logarithmic differentiation.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.power-series-convergence.stewart.notes: Stewart sketches the proof: if the series converges at x = d ≠ a, then cₙdⁿ is bounded, say |cₙdⁿ| ≤ M. For |x| < |d|, we have |cₙxⁿ| ≤ M|x/d|ⁿ, a convergent geometric series. The radius of convergence is then R = sup{|x-a| : series converges}. Full details of the supremum argument are omitted.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.power-series-differentiation-integ.notes: Stewart states this theorem without proof, noting it requires uniform convergence concepts from advanced analysis. The proof that term-by-term differentiation preserves convergence and yields the correct derivative requires the Weierstrass M-test and uniform convergence of the differentiated series.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.product-rule.stewart.notes: Add and subtract f(x+h)g(x): [f(x+h)g(x+h) - f(x)g(x)]/h = f(x+h)[g(x+h)-g(x)]/h + g(x)[f(x+h)-f(x)]/h. As h→0, f(x+h)→f(x) (by continuity, since f is differentiable), yielding f(x)g'(x) + g(x)f'(x).

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.quotient-rule.stewart.notes: [f(x+h)/g(x+h) - f(x)/g(x)]/h = [f(x+h)g(x) - f(x)g(x+h)] / [h · g(x+h)g(x)]. Add and subtract f(x)g(x) in the numerator, apply limit laws, and use continuity of g to get g(x+h)→g(x).

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.ratio-test.stewart.notes: Part (i): If L < 1, pick r with L < r < 1. For large n, |aₙ₊₁/aₙ| < r, so |aₙ| < |aₙ|rⁿ⁻ᴺ for n ≥ N. By comparison with a convergent geometric series, ∑ |aₙ| converges. Part (ii): For large n, |aₙ₊₁| > |aₙ|, so aₙ does not approach 0; the series diverges by the Divergence Test.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.rolles-theorem.stewart.notes: Case 1: f(x) = f(a) for all x in [a,b], then f is constant and f'(c) = 0 for any c. Case 2: f(x) > f(a) for some x, then by EVT f attains a maximum at some c in (a,b) (not an endpoint since f(a) = f(b)). By Fermat's theorem, f'(c) = 0. Case 3: analogous with minimum.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.root-test.stewart.notes: Part (i): If L < 1, pick r with L < r < 1. For large n, ⁿ√|aₙ| < r, so |aₙ| < rⁿ. By comparison with the convergent geometric series ∑ rⁿ, the series ∑ |aₙ| converges.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.second-derivative-test.stewart.notes: If f'(c) = 0 and f''(c) > 0, then f is concave up near c. Since the tangent line at c is horizontal (slope 0) and the curve is above the tangent, c is a local minimum. Analogous for max.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.squeeze-theorem.stewart.notes: Given epsilon > 0, since lim f(x) = L and lim h(x) = L, there exist delta_1 and delta_2 such that f(x) and h(x) are within epsilon of L. Taking delta = min(delta_1, delta_2), the inequality f(x) <= g(x) <= h(x) forces g(x) within epsilon of L.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.substitution-rule-definite.stewart.notes: Let F be an antiderivative of f. Then by FTC Part 2: ∫_a^b f(g(x))g'(x)dx = F(g(x))|_a^b = F(g(b)) - F(g(a)) = ∫_{g(a)}^{g(b)} f(u)du.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.substitution-rule.stewart.notes: If F is an antiderivative of f, then by the chain rule d/dx[F(g(x))] = F'(g(x)) g'(x) = f(g(x)) g'(x). Therefore ∫ f(g(x)) g'(x) dx = F(g(x)) + C = F(u) + C = ∫ f(u) du.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.sum-rule.stewart.notes: d/dx[f(x)+g(x)] = lim(h→0) {[f(x+h)+g(x+h)] - [f(x)+g(x)]}/h = lim(h→0) [f(x+h)-f(x)]/h + lim(h→0) [g(x+h)-g(x)]/h = f'(x) + g'(x) by the sum law for limits.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.taylor-convergence.stewart.notes: Taylor's inequality |Rₙ(x)| ≤ M|x-a|ⁿ⁺¹/(n+1)! is derived from the Lagrange form of the remainder (which uses the MVT applied to the remainder function). Since |x-a|ⁿ⁺¹/(n+1)! → 0 for any fixed x (by the Squeeze Theorem, comparing with the convergent series for eˣ), we get Rₙ(x) → 0.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.vertical-line-test.stewart.notes: Stewart argues directly from the definition of function: if a vertical line x = a intersects the curve at two points, then the curve assigns two values to a, contradicting the definition of function.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proof.zero-derivative-constant.stewart.notes: For any x1 < x2 in (a,b), MVT gives f(x2) - f(x1) = f'(c)(x2-x1) for some c in (x1,x2). Since f'(c) = 0, f(x2) = f(x1).

sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: If f is a one-to-one function with inverse f⁻¹, then f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for every x in the domain of f, and f(f⁻¹(x)) = x for every x in the domain of f⁻¹.
natural.es: Si f es una función inyectiva con inversa f⁻¹, entonces f⁻¹(f(x)) = x para todo x en el dominio de f, y f(f⁻¹(x)) = x para todo x en el dominio de f⁻¹.

proposition.cancellation-equations.notes: Stewart presents the cancellation equations as direct consequences of the definition of inverse function in section 1.5.

natural.en: For any positive number a ≠ 1, we have logₐx = ln(x)/ln(a) for all x > 0.
natural.es: Para cualquier número positivo a ≠ 1, se tiene logₐx = ln(x)/ln(a) para todo x > 0.

proposition.change-of-base-formula.notes: Stewart presents the change of base formula in section 1.5, noting it allows computing any logarithm using natural logarithms.

sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: (a) If f''(x) > 0 for all x in I, then the graph of f is concave upward on I. (b) If f''(x) < 0 for all x in I, then the graph of f is concave downward on I.
natural.es: (a) Si f''(x) > 0 para toda x en I, entonces la gráfica de f es cóncava hacia arriba en I. (b) Si f''(x) < 0 para toda x en I, entonces la gráfica de f es cóncava hacia abajo en I.

proposition.concavity-test.notes: f'' > 0 means f' is increasing, so the slope of the tangent line is increasing, hence the curve lies above its tangents.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: If f is a polynomial or rational function and a is in the domain of f, then lim(x→a) f(x) = f(a).
natural.es: Si f es una función polinomial o racional y a está en el dominio de f, entonces lim(x→a) f(x) = f(a).

proposition.direct-substitution-property.notes: Stewart derives this from the limit laws. It is the basis for direct evaluation of limits for polynomial and rational functions.

natural.en: Suppose that c is a critical number of a continuous function f. (a) If f' changes from positive to negative at c, then f has a local maximum at c. (b) If f' changes from negative to positive at c, then f has a local minimum at c. (c) If f' does not change sign at c, then f has no local extremum at c.
natural.es: Suponga que c es un número crítico de una función continua f. (a) Si f' cambia de positiva a negativa en c, entonces f tiene un máximo local en c. (b) Si f' cambia de negativa a positiva en c, entonces f tiene un mínimo local en c. (c) Si f' no cambia de signo en c, entonces f no tiene extremo local en c.

proposition.first-derivative-test.notes: Follows from the increasing/decreasing test applied to intervals on either side of the critical number.

natural.en: A function is one-to-one if and only if no horizontal line intersects its graph more than once.
natural.es: Una función es inyectiva si y sólo si ninguna línea horizontal corta su gráfica más de una vez.

proposition.horizontal-line-test.notes: Reclassified from definition to proposition. The horizontal line test is a criterion for injectivity, not the introduction of a new mathematical object.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: (a) If f'(x) > 0 on an interval, then f is increasing on that interval. (b) If f'(x) < 0 on an interval, then f is decreasing on that interval.
natural.es: (a) Si f'(x) > 0 en un intervalo, entonces f es creciente en ese intervalo. (b) Si f'(x) < 0 en un intervalo, entonces f es decreciente en ese intervalo.

proposition.increasing-decreasing-test.notes: Direct consequence of the Mean Value Theorem.

natural.en: If f and g are integrable on [a, b]: 1. If f(x) ≥ 0 for a ≤ x ≤ b, then ∫_a^b f(x) dx ≥ 0. 2. If f(x) ≥ g(x) for a ≤ x ≤ b, then ∫_a^b f(x) dx ≥ ∫_a^b g(x) dx. 3. If m ≤ f(x) ≤ M for a ≤ x ≤ b, then m(b-a) ≤ ∫_a^b f(x) dx ≤ M(b-a).
natural.es: Si f y g son integrables en [a, b]: 1. Si f(x) ≥ 0 para a ≤ x ≤ b, entonces ∫_a^b f(x) dx ≥ 0. 2. Si f(x) ≥ g(x) para a ≤ x ≤ b, entonces ∫_a^b f(x) dx ≥ ∫_a^b g(x) dx. 3. Si m ≤ f(x) ≤ M para a ≤ x ≤ b, entonces m(b-a) ≤ ∫_a^b f(x) dx ≤ M(b-a).

proposition.integral-comparison.notes: Follow from the definition: non-negative integrands produce non-negative Riemann sums, and limits preserve inequalities.

title.es: Propiedades de comparación de la integral

natural.en: Let f and g be integrable functions and c a constant. Then: 1. ∫_a^b c dx = c(b - a). 2. ∫_a^b [f(x) + g(x)] dx = ∫_a^b f(x) dx + ∫_a^b g(x) dx. 3. ∫_a^b cf(x) dx = c ∫_a^b f(x) dx. 4. ∫_a^b [f(x) - g(x)] dx = ∫_a^b f(x) dx - ∫_a^b g(x) dx. 5. ∫_a^c f(x) dx + ∫_c^b f(x) dx = ∫_a^b f(x) dx.
natural.es: Sean f y g funciones integrables y c una constante. Entonces: 1. ∫_a^b c dx = c(b - a). 2. ∫_a^b [f(x) + g(x)] dx = ∫_a^b f(x) dx + ∫_a^b g(x) dx. 3. ∫_a^b cf(x) dx = c ∫_a^b f(x) dx. 4. ∫_a^b [f(x) - g(x)] dx = ∫_a^b f(x) dx - ∫_a^b g(x) dx. 5. ∫_a^c f(x) dx + ∫_c^b f(x) dx = ∫_a^b f(x) dx.

proposition.integral-properties.notes: These properties follow from the linearity of limits and the definition of the definite integral as a limit of Riemann sums.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proposition.integrals-symmetric-function.latex:
f \text{ even} \;\Rightarrow\; \int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx = 2\int_0^a f(x)\,dx \\
f \text{ odd} \;\Rightarrow\; \int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx = 0

natural.en: Suppose f is continuous on [-a, a]. (a) If f is even [f(-x) = f(x)], then ∫_{-a}^{a} f(x) dx = 2 ∫_0^a f(x) dx. (b) If f is odd [f(-x) = -f(x)], then ∫_{-a}^{a} f(x) dx = 0.
natural.es: Suponga que f es continua en [-a, a]. (a) Si f es par [f(-x) = f(x)], entonces ∫_{-a}^{a} f(x) dx = 2 ∫_0^a f(x) dx. (b) Si f es impar [f(-x) = -f(x)], entonces ∫_{-a}^{a} f(x) dx = 0.

proposition.integrals-symmetric-function.notes: Proved using the substitution u = -x on the integral from -a to 0.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: The linear differential equation dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) is solved by multiplying both sides by the integrating factor I(x) = e^{∫P(x)dx}. The solution is y = (1/I(x)) ∫ I(x)Q(x) dx.
natural.es: La ecuación diferencial lineal dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) se resuelve multiplicando ambos lados por el factor integrante I(x) = e^{∫P(x)dx}. La solución es y = (1/I(x)) ∫ I(x)Q(x) dx.

proposition.integrating-factor-method.notes: The integrating factor transforms the left side into the derivative of a product: d/dx[I(x)y] = I(x)Q(x). This is then integrated using the FTC.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: If f is a one-to-one function, then the graph of f⁻¹ is obtained by reflecting the graph of f about the line y = x.
natural.es: Si f es una función inyectiva, entonces la gráfica de f⁻¹ se obtiene reflejando la gráfica de f respecto a la recta y = x.

proposition.inverse-graph-reflection.notes: Stewart derives this geometric property from the fact that (a,b) is on the graph of f if and only if (b,a) is on the graph of f⁻¹.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

title.es: Gráfica de la inversa como reflexión

proposition.laws-of-exponents.latex: a^{x+y} = a^x a^y, \quad a^{x-y} = \frac{a^x}{a^y}, \quad (a^x)^y = a^{xy}, \quad (ab)^x = a^x b^x

natural.en: If a and b are positive numbers and x, y are any real numbers, then the following laws hold: (1) aˣ⁺ʸ = aˣaʸ, (2) aˣ⁻ʸ = aˣ/aʸ, (3) (aˣ)ʸ = aˣʸ, (4) (ab)ˣ = aˣbˣ.
natural.es: Si a y b son números positivos y x, y son números reales cualesquiera, entonces se cumplen las siguientes leyes: (1) aˣ⁺ʸ = aˣaʸ, (2) aˣ⁻ʸ = aˣ/aʸ, (3) (aˣ)ʸ = aˣʸ, (4) (ab)ˣ = aˣbˣ.

proposition.laws-of-exponents.notes: Stewart states the laws of exponents in section 1.4 without proof, treating them as known results from precalculus extended to real exponents.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proposition.laws-of-logarithms.latex: \log_a(xy) = \log_a x + \log_a y, \quad \log_a\!\left(\frac{x}{y}\right) = \log_a x - \log_a y, \quad \log_a(x^r) = r \log_a x

natural.en: If x > 0 and y > 0, then: (1) logₐ(xy) = logₐx + logₐy, (2) logₐ(x/y) = logₐx - logₐy, (3) logₐ(xʳ) = r logₐx for any real number r.
natural.es: Si x > 0 e y > 0, entonces: (1) logₐ(xy) = logₐx + logₐy, (2) logₐ(x/y) = logₐx - logₐy, (3) logₐ(xʳ) = r logₐx para todo número real r.

proposition.laws-of-logarithms.notes: Stewart derives the laws of logarithms in section 1.5 from the corresponding laws of exponents.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

proposition.limit-exists-iff-one-sided-l.latex: \lim_{x \to a} f(x) = L \iff \lim_{x \to a^-} f(x) = L \;\text{ and }\; \lim_{x \to a^+} f(x) = L

natural.en: lim(x→a) f(x) = L if and only if lim(x→a⁻) f(x) = L and lim(x→a⁺) f(x) = L.
natural.es: lim(x→a) f(x) = L si y sólo si lim(x→a⁻) f(x) = L y lim(x→a⁺) f(x) = L.

proposition.limit-exists-iff-one-sided-l.notes: Stewart states this as a fundamental criterion in section 2.2. The proof follows from the epsilon-delta definition in 2.4.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

title.en: Limit exists if and only if one-sided limits agree
title.es: El límite existe si y sólo si los límites laterales coinciden

natural.en: If f has a local extremum at c, then c is a critical number of f.
natural.es: Si f tiene un extremo local en c, entonces c es un número crítico de f.

proposition.local-extremum-at-critical.notes: Direct consequence of Fermat's theorem: if f'(c) exists then f'(c) = 0, and if f'(c) does not exist, c is still a critical number by definition.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

title.en: Local extrema occur at critical numbers
title.es: Los extremos locales ocurren en números críticos

proposition.second-derivative-test.latex:
f'(c) = 0 \;\wedge\; f''(c) > 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{local min at } c \\
f'(c) = 0 \;\wedge\; f''(c) < 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{local max at } c

natural.en: Suppose f'' is continuous near c. (a) If f'(c) = 0 and f''(c) > 0, then f has a local minimum at c. (b) If f'(c) = 0 and f''(c) < 0, then f has a local maximum at c.
natural.es: Suponga que f'' es continua cerca de c. (a) Si f'(c) = 0 y f''(c) > 0, entonces f tiene un mínimo local en c. (b) Si f'(c) = 0 y f''(c) < 0, entonces f tiene un máximo local en c.

proposition.second-derivative-test.notes: When f''(c) > 0, f is concave up near c, so the tangent line at c lies below the graph, meaning c is a local minimum.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: A curve in the xy-plane is the graph of a function of x if and only if no vertical line intersects the curve more than once.
natural.es: Una curva en el plano xy es la gráfica de una función de x si y sólo si ninguna línea vertical corta a la curva en más de un punto.

proposition.vertical-line-test.notes: Reclassified from definition to proposition. The vertical line test is a criterion for determining whether a curve represents a function, not the introduction of a new mathematical object.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: If a series ∑ aₙ is absolutely convergent, then it is convergent.
natural.es: Si una serie ∑ aₙ es absolutamente convergente, entonces es convergente.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: If the alternating series ∑_{n=1}^∞ (-1)ⁿ⁻¹ bₙ (with bₙ > 0) satisfies (i) bₙ₊₁ ≤ bₙ for all n and (ii) lim(n→∞) bₙ = 0, then the series converges.
natural.es: Si la serie alternante ∑_{n=1}^∞ (-1)ⁿ⁻¹ bₙ (con bₙ > 0) satisface (i) bₙ₊₁ ≤ bₙ para todo n y (ii) lim(n→∞) bₙ = 0, entonces la serie converge.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: If g is differentiable at x and f is differentiable at g(x), then the composite function F = f ∘ g defined by F(x) = f(g(x)) is differentiable at x and F' is given by F'(x) = f'(g(x)) · g'(x). In Leibniz notation, if y = f(u) and u = g(x) are differentiable functions, then dy/dx = (dy/du)(du/dx).
natural.es: Si g es diferenciable en x y f es diferenciable en g(x), entonces la función compuesta F = f ∘ g definida por F(x) = f(g(x)) es diferenciable en x y F' se obtiene mediante F'(x) = f'(g(x)) · g'(x). En notación de Leibniz, si y = f(u) y u = g(x) son funciones diferenciables, entonces dy/dx = (dy/du)(du/dx).

theorem.chain-rule.notes: One of the most important rules in calculus. Stewart proves it using an increment formulation that avoids dividing by Δu = 0.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: Suppose ∑ aₙ and ∑ bₙ are series with positive terms. (i) If ∑ bₙ converges and aₙ ≤ bₙ for all n, then ∑ aₙ also converges. (ii) If ∑ bₙ diverges and aₙ ≥ bₙ for all n, then ∑ aₙ also diverges.
natural.es: Suponga que ∑ aₙ y ∑ bₙ son series con términos positivos. (i) Si ∑ bₙ converge y aₙ ≤ bₙ para todo n, entonces ∑ aₙ también converge. (ii) Si ∑ bₙ diverge y aₙ ≥ bₙ para todo n, entonces ∑ aₙ también diverge.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: Suppose f and g are continuous functions with f(x) ≥ g(x) ≥ 0 for x ≥ a. (a) If ∫_a^∞ f(x) dx is convergent, then ∫_a^∞ g(x) dx is also convergent. (b) If ∫_a^∞ g(x) dx is divergent, then ∫_a^∞ f(x) dx is also divergent.
natural.es: Suponga que f y g son funciones continuas con f(x) ≥ g(x) ≥ 0 para x ≥ a. (a) Si ∫_a^∞ f(x) dx es convergente, entonces ∫_a^∞ g(x) dx también es convergente. (b) Si ∫_a^∞ g(x) dx es divergente, entonces ∫_a^∞ f(x) dx también es divergente.

theorem.comparison-theorem-integrals.notes: The comparison theorem is analogous to the comparison test for series (Chapter 11). Stewart states it without detailed proof, relying on the monotone convergence property of bounded increasing sequences.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

title.es: Teorema de comparación para integrales impropias

natural.en: If c is a constant and f is a differentiable function, then d/dx[cf(x)] = c d/dx f(x).
natural.es: Si c es una constante y f es una función diferenciable, entonces d/dx[cf(x)] = c d/dx f(x).

theorem.constant-multiple-rule.notes: Proved using the definition of the derivative and the constant multiple law for limits.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: If f and g are continuous at a and c is a constant, then the following functions are also continuous at a: f + g, f - g, cf, fg, and f/g (if g(a) ≠ 0).
natural.es: Si f y g son continuas en a y c es una constante, entonces las siguientes funciones también son continuas en a: f + g, f - g, cf, fg, y f/g (si g(a) ≠ 0).

theorem.continuity-of-combinations.notes: Follows directly from the limit laws applied to the definition of continuity.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: If f is continuous at b and lim(x→a) g(x) = b, then lim(x→a) f(g(x)) = f(b). In other words, lim(x→a) f(g(x)) = f(lim(x→a) g(x)). In particular, if g is continuous at a and f is continuous at g(a), then the composite function f ∘ g is continuous at a.
natural.es: Si f es continua en b y lim(x→a) g(x) = b, entonces lim(x→a) f(g(x)) = f(b). En otras palabras, lim(x→a) f(g(x)) = f(lim(x→a) g(x)). En particular, si g es continua en a y f es continua en g(a), entonces la función compuesta f ∘ g es continua en a.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: d/dx(cos⁻¹ x) = -1/√(1 - x²), for -1 < x < 1.
natural.es: d/dx(cos⁻¹ x) = -1/√(1 - x²), para -1 < x < 1.

theorem.derivative-arccos.notes: Similar to arcsin: if y = cos⁻¹ x then cos y = x, so -sin y · dy/dx = 1, giving dy/dx = -1/sin y = -1/√(1 - x²).

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: d/dx(sin⁻¹ x) = 1/√(1 - x²), for -1 < x < 1.
natural.es: d/dx(sin⁻¹ x) = 1/√(1 - x²), para -1 < x < 1.

theorem.derivative-arcsin.notes: Derived via implicit differentiation: if y = sin⁻¹ x then sin y = x, so cos y · dy/dx = 1, giving dy/dx = 1/cos y = 1/√(1 - sin²y) = 1/√(1 - x²).

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: d/dx(tan⁻¹ x) = 1/(1 + x²).
natural.es: d/dx(tan⁻¹ x) = 1/(1 + x²).

theorem.derivative-arctan.notes: If y = tan⁻¹ x then tan y = x, so sec²y · dy/dx = 1, giving dy/dx = 1/sec²y = 1/(1 + tan²y) = 1/(1 + x²).

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: The derivative of a constant function is 0. That is, d/dx(c) = 0.
natural.es: La derivada de una función constante es 0. Es decir, d/dx(c) = 0.

theorem.derivative-constant.notes: Follows directly from the definition of the derivative: the difference quotient (f(x+h) - f(x))/h = (c - c)/h = 0 for all h.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: d/dx(cos x) = -sin x.
natural.es: d/dx(cos x) = -sin x.

theorem.derivative-cos.notes: Proved similarly to sin, using the addition formula for cosine and the same two special limits.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: d/dx(cot x) = -csc²x.
natural.es: d/dx(cot x) = -csc²x.

theorem.derivative-cot.notes: cot x = cos x / sin x. Apply the quotient rule using d/dx(sin x) = cos x and d/dx(cos x) = -sin x.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: d/dx(csc x) = -csc x cot x.
natural.es: d/dx(csc x) = -csc x cot x.

theorem.derivative-csc.notes: csc x = 1/sin x. Apply the quotient rule (or reciprocal rule) using d/dx(sin x) = cos x.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: e = lim(x→0) (1 + x)^{1/x}. This formula is a consequence of the derivative of ln x evaluated at x = 1.
natural.es: e = lim(x→0) (1 + x)^{1/x}. Esta fórmula es consecuencia de la derivada de ln x evaluada en x = 1.

theorem.derivative-e-formula.notes: Stewart derives this from ln'(1) = 1: lim(x→0) [ln(1+x)]/x = 1, so lim(x→0) ln(1+x)^{1/x} = 1, hence (1+x)^{1/x} → e.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

title.en: The number e as a limit

natural.en: d/dx(e^x) = e^x. The natural exponential function is its own derivative.
natural.es: d/dx(e^x) = e^x. La función exponencial natural es su propia derivada.

theorem.derivative-exponential.notes: Follows from the definition of e as the base for which lim(h→0)(e^h - 1)/h = 1 and the definition of the derivative.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: d/dx(a^x) = a^x ln a, for a > 0, a ≠ 1.
natural.es: d/dx(a^x) = a^x ln a, para a > 0, a ≠ 1.

theorem.derivative-general-exponential.notes: Since a^x = e^{x ln a}, apply the chain rule: d/dx(e^{x ln a}) = e^{x ln a} · ln a = a^x ln a.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

title.es: Derivada de la función exponencial general

natural.en: d/dx(ln x) = 1/x, for x > 0.
natural.es: d/dx(ln x) = 1/x, para x > 0.

theorem.derivative-ln.notes: Derived via implicit differentiation: if y = ln x then e^y = x, so e^y · dy/dx = 1, giving dy/dx = 1/e^y = 1/x.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: d/dx(ln|x|) = 1/x, for x ≠ 0.
natural.es: d/dx(ln|x|) = 1/x, para x ≠ 0.

theorem.derivative-ln-abs.notes: For x > 0, ln|x| = ln x so d/dx = 1/x. For x < 0, ln|x| = ln(-x) so d/dx = (1/(-x))·(-1) = 1/x by the chain rule.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: d/dx(log_a x) = 1/(x ln a), for x > 0, a > 0, a ≠ 1.
natural.es: d/dx(log_a x) = 1/(x ln a), para x > 0, a > 0, a ≠ 1.

theorem.derivative-log-base-a.notes: Follows from the change of base formula log_a x = ln x / ln a and the derivative of ln x.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

title.es: Derivada del logaritmo en base a

natural.en: d/dx(sec x) = sec x tan x.
natural.es: d/dx(sec x) = sec x tan x.

theorem.derivative-sec.notes: sec x = 1/cos x. Apply the quotient rule using d/dx(cos x) = -sin x.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: d/dx(sin x) = cos x.
natural.es: d/dx(sin x) = cos x.

theorem.derivative-sin.notes: Stewart proves this from the definition of the derivative using the addition formula for sine and the special limits sin(h)/h → 1 and (cos h - 1)/h → 0.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: d/dx(tan x) = sec²x.
natural.es: d/dx(tan x) = sec²x.

theorem.derivative-tan.notes: tan x = sin x / cos x. Apply the quotient rule using d/dx(sin x) = cos x and d/dx(cos x) = -sin x.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

theorem.differentiable-implies-continuou.latex: f \text{ diferenciable en } a \implies f \text{ continua en } a

natural.en: If f is differentiable at a, then f is continuous at a.
natural.es: Si f es diferenciable en a, entonces f es continua en a.

theorem.differentiable-implies-continuou.notes: Stewart proves this theorem in section 2.8. The converse is false: f(x) = |x| is continuous at 0 but not differentiable there.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: If lim(n→∞) aₙ does not exist or if lim(n→∞) aₙ ≠ 0, then the series ∑ aₙ diverges.
natural.es: Si lim(n→∞) aₙ no existe o si lim(n→∞) aₙ ≠ 0, entonces la serie ∑ aₙ diverge.

theorem.divergence-test.notes: The converse is false: lim aₙ = 0 does not imply convergence (e.g., the harmonic series).

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: If f is continuous on a closed interval [a, b], then f attains an absolute maximum value f(c) and an absolute minimum value f(d) at some numbers c and d in [a, b].
natural.es: Si f es continua en un intervalo cerrado [a, b], entonces f alcanza un valor máximo absoluto f(c) y un valor mínimo absoluto f(d) en algún par de números c y d en [a, b].

theorem.extreme-value-theorem.notes: Stewart states this theorem without proof. The proof requires the completeness of the real numbers (Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem or equivalent). It depends on continuity on a closed interval.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

theorem.fermat-theorem.latex:
f \text{ has local extremum at } c \;\wedge\; f'(c) \text{ exists}
\;\Rightarrow\; f'(c) = 0

natural.en: If f has a local maximum or minimum at c, and f'(c) exists, then f'(c) = 0.
natural.es: Si f tiene un máximo o mínimo local en c y f'(c) existe, entonces f'(c) = 0.

theorem.fermat-theorem.notes: Stewart proves this by analyzing one-sided limits of the difference quotient at a local maximum. The key lemma for Rolle's theorem and the Mean Value Theorem.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: If f is continuous on [a, b], then the function g defined by g(x) = ∫_a^x f(t) dt, for a ≤ x ≤ b, is continuous on [a, b] and differentiable on (a, b), and g'(x) = f(x).
natural.es: Si f es continua en [a, b], entonces la función g definida por g(x) = ∫_a^x f(t) dt, con a ≤ x ≤ b, es continua en [a, b] y derivable en (a, b), y g'(x) = f(x).

theorem.ftc-part1.notes: FTC Part 1 establishes that differentiation and integration are inverse processes. It says that every continuous function has an antiderivative, and provides a way to construct it.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

title.en: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, Part 1

natural.en: If f is continuous on [a, b], then ∫_a^b f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a), where F is any antiderivative of f, that is, a function such that F' = f.
natural.es: Si f es continua en [a, b], entonces ∫_a^b f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a), donde F es cualquier antiderivada de f, es decir, una función tal que F' = f.

theorem.ftc-part2.notes: FTC Part 2 (the Evaluation Theorem) provides the practical method for computing definite integrals. Stewart often writes F(b) - F(a) = F(x)|_a^b = [F(x)]_a^b.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

title.en: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, Part 2

natural.en: If F is an antiderivative of f on an interval I, then the most general antiderivative of f on I is F(x) + C, where C is an arbitrary constant.
natural.es: Si F es una antiderivada de f en un intervalo I, entonces la antiderivada más general de f en I es F(x) + C, donde C es una constante arbitraria.

theorem.general-antiderivative.notes: Direct consequence of the corollary that functions with equal derivatives differ by a constant.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: The geometric series ∑_{n=1}^∞ arⁿ⁻¹ = a + ar + ar² + ... converges if |r| < 1 and its sum is a/(1-r). If |r| ≥ 1, the series diverges.
natural.es: La serie geométrica ∑_{n=1}^∞ arⁿ⁻¹ = a + ar + ar² + ... converge si |r| < 1 y su suma es a/(1-r). Si |r| ≥ 1, la serie diverge.

sources.author: James Stewart
sources.work: Cálculo de una variable — Trascendentes tempranas

natural.en: If f is continuous on [a, b], or if f has only a finite number of jump discontinuities, then f is integrable on [a, b]; that is, the definite integral ∫_a^b f(x)dx exists.
natural.es: Si f es continua en [a, b], o si f tiene sólo un número finito de discontinuidades de salto, entonces f es integrable en [a, b]; es decir, la integral definida ∫_a^b f(x)dx existe.

theorem.integrability-of-continuous-func.notes: Stewart states this without proof. A rigorous proof requires the uniform continuity theorem (which follows from the completeness of the reals).

natural.en: Suppose f is a continuous, positive, decreasing function on [1, ∞) and let aₙ = f(n). Then the series ∑_{n=1}^∞ aₙ converges if and only if the improper integral ∫_1^∞ f(x) dx converges.
natural.es: Suponga que f es una función continua, positiva y decreciente en [1, ∞) y sea aₙ = f(n). Entonces la serie ∑_{n=1}^∞ aₙ converge si y sólo si la integral impropia ∫_1^∞ f(x) dx converge.

natural.en: If f and g are differentiable, then ∫ f(x)g'(x) dx = f(x)g(x) - ∫ g(x)f'(x) dx. Using the notation u = f(x), v = g(x): ∫ u dv = uv - ∫ v du.
natural.es: Si f y g son diferenciables, entonces ∫ f(x)g'(x) dx = f(x)g(x) - ∫ g(x)f'(x) dx. Con la notación u = f(x), v = g(x): ∫ u dv = uv - ∫ v du.

theorem.integration-by-parts.notes: The integration counterpart of the product rule. Stewart derives it by integrating both sides of the product rule and rearranging.

natural.en: If f and g are differentiable and their derivatives are continuous on [a, b], then ∫_a^b f(x)g'(x) dx = [f(x)g(x)]_a^b - ∫_a^b g(x)f'(x) dx.
natural.es: Si f y g son diferenciables y sus derivadas son continuas en [a, b], entonces ∫_a^b f(x)g'(x) dx = [f(x)g(x)]_a^b - ∫_a^b g(x)f'(x) dx.

theorem.integration-by-parts-definite.notes: The definite integral version of integration by parts. Follows from applying FTC Part 2 to the indefinite integration by parts formula.

theorem.intermediate-value-theorem.latex: f \text{ continua en } [a,b], \; N \text{ entre } f(a) \text{ y } f(b) \implies \exists\, c \in (a,b) : f(c) = N

natural.en: Suppose that f is continuous on the closed interval [a, b] and let N be any number between f(a) and f(b), where f(a) ≠ f(b). Then there exists a number c in (a, b) such that f(c) = N.
natural.es: Suponga que f es continua en el intervalo cerrado [a, b] y sea N cualquier número entre f(a) y f(b), donde f(a) ≠ f(b). Entonces existe un número c en (a, b) tal que f(c) = N.

theorem.intermediate-value-theorem.notes: Stewart states the IVT without proof in section 2.5, noting that a proof based on the completeness axiom of the real numbers can be found in Appendix F. It is used extensively for existence proofs (e.g., showing a root exists in an interval).

natural.en: Suppose that f and g are differentiable and g'(x) ≠ 0 near a (except possibly at a). Suppose that lim(x→a) f(x) = 0 and lim(x→a) g(x) = 0, or that lim(x→a) f(x) = ±∞ and lim(x→a) g(x) = ±∞ (i.e., we have an indeterminate form of type 0/0 or ∞/∞). Then lim(x→a) f(x)/g(x) = lim(x→a) f'(x)/g'(x), if the limit on the right side exists (or is ±∞).
natural.es: Suponga que f y g son derivables y que g'(x) ≠ 0 cerca de a (excepto posiblemente en a). Suponga que lim(x→a) f(x) = 0 y lim(x→a) g(x) = 0, o que lim(x→a) f(x) = ±∞ y lim(x→a) g(x) = ±∞ (es decir, que se tiene una forma indeterminada 0/0 o ∞/∞). Entonces lim(x→a) f(x)/g(x) = lim(x→a) f'(x)/g'(x), si el límite del lado derecho existe (o es ±∞).

theorem.lhopitals-rule.notes: Stewart proves the 0/0 case using the Cauchy Mean Value Theorem (a generalization of MVT). The ∞/∞ case is stated without complete proof. The rule also applies to one-sided limits and limits at infinity.

natural.en: Suppose ∑ aₙ and ∑ bₙ are series with positive terms. If lim(n→∞) aₙ/bₙ = c, where c is a finite number and c > 0, then either both series converge or both diverge.
natural.es: Suponga que ∑ aₙ y ∑ bₙ son series con términos positivos. Si lim(n→∞) aₙ/bₙ = c, donde c es un número finito y c > 0, entonces ambas series convergen o ambas divergen.

theorem.limit-laws.latex:
\begin{aligned}
&\lim_{x \to a} [f(x) + g(x)] = \lim_{x \to a} f(x) + \lim_{x \to a} g(x) \\
&\lim_{x \to a} [f(x) - g(x)] = \lim_{x \to a} f(x) - \lim_{x \to a} g(x) \\
&\lim_{x \to a} [c \cdot f(x)] = c \cdot \lim_{x \to a} f(x) \\
&\lim_{x \to a} [f(x) \cdot g(x)] = \lim_{x \to a} f(x) \cdot \lim_{x \to a} g(x) \\
&\lim_{x \to a} \frac{f(x)}{g(x)} = \frac{\lim_{x \to a} f(x)}{\lim_{x \to a} g(x)} \quad \text{si } \lim_{x \to a} g(x) \neq 0
\end{aligned}

natural.en: Suppose that c is a constant and the limits lim(x→a) f(x) and lim(x→a) g(x) exist. Then: 1. lim(x→a) [f(x) + g(x)] = lim(x→a) f(x) + lim(x→a) g(x), 2. lim(x→a) [f(x) - g(x)] = lim(x→a) f(x) - lim(x→a) g(x), 3. lim(x→a) [cf(x)] = c lim(x→a) f(x), 4. lim(x→a) [f(x)g(x)] = lim(x→a) f(x) · lim(x→a) g(x), 5. lim(x→a) [f(x)/g(x)] = lim(x→a) f(x) / lim(x→a) g(x), provided lim(x→a) g(x) ≠ 0.
natural.es: Suponga que c es una constante y que los límites lim(x→a) f(x) y lim(x→a) g(x) existen. Entonces: 1. lim(x→a) [f(x) + g(x)] = lim(x→a) f(x) + lim(x→a) g(x), 2. lim(x→a) [f(x) - g(x)] = lim(x→a) f(x) - lim(x→a) g(x), 3. lim(x→a) [cf(x)] = c lim(x→a) f(x), 4. lim(x→a) [f(x)g(x)] = lim(x→a) f(x) · lim(x→a) g(x), 5. lim(x→a) [f(x)/g(x)] = lim(x→a) f(x) / lim(x→a) g(x), si lim(x→a) g(x) ≠ 0.

theorem.limit-laws.notes: Stewart presents these as the fundamental laws for computing limits. The proofs use the epsilon-delta definition from section 2.4.

natural.en: lim(x→∞) 1/xʳ = 0 and lim(x→-∞) 1/xʳ = 0 if r > 0 is a rational number and xʳ is defined for all x.
natural.es: lim(x→∞) 1/xʳ = 0 y lim(x→-∞) 1/xʳ = 0 si r > 0 es un número racional y xʳ está definido para todo x.

theorem.limit-one-over-x-at-infinity.notes: This is the fundamental building block for evaluating limits at infinity of rational functions by dividing numerator and denominator by the highest power of x.

natural.en: If lim(x→a) f(x) exists and n is a positive integer, then lim(x→a) [f(x)]ⁿ = [lim(x→a) f(x)]ⁿ.
natural.es: Si lim(x→a) f(x) existe y n es un entero positivo, entonces lim(x→a) [f(x)]ⁿ = [lim(x→a) f(x)]ⁿ.

theorem.limit-power-law.notes: Follows from repeated application of the product law (law 4 of the limit laws).

natural.en: If lim(x→a) f(x) exists and n is a positive integer, then lim(x→a) ⁿ√f(x) = ⁿ√(lim(x→a) f(x)). If n is even, we require that lim(x→a) f(x) > 0.
natural.es: Si lim(x→a) f(x) existe y n es un entero positivo, entonces lim(x→a) ⁿ√f(x) = ⁿ√(lim(x→a) f(x)). Si n es par, se requiere que lim(x→a) f(x) > 0.

natural.en: The limit of sin(x)/x as x approaches 0 equals 1.
natural.es: El límite de sen(x)/x cuando x tiende a 0 es igual a 1.

theorem.limit-sinx-over-x.notes: Stewart proves this using the squeeze theorem with a geometric argument involving areas of sectors and triangles in the unit circle. This result is essential for differentiating trigonometric functions.

natural.en: Let f be a function that satisfies the following hypotheses: 1. f is continuous on the closed interval [a, b]. 2. f is differentiable on the open interval (a, b). Then there is a number c in (a, b) such that f'(c) = (f(b) - f(a)) / (b - a), or equivalently, f(b) - f(a) = f'(c)(b - a).
natural.es: Sea f una función que satisface las dos hipótesis siguientes: 1. f es continua en el intervalo cerrado [a, b]. 2. f es derivable en el intervalo abierto (a, b). Entonces existe un número c en (a, b) tal que f'(c) = (f(b) - f(a)) / (b - a), o equivalentemente, f(b) - f(a) = f'(c)(b - a).

theorem.mean-value-theorem.notes: One of the most important theorems in calculus. Stewart proves it by applying Rolle's theorem to the auxiliary function h(x) = f(x) - [f(a) + ((f(b)-f(a))/(b-a))(x-a)].

\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = f(c)(b - a)
\quad\text{for some } c \in [a, b]

natural.en: If f is continuous on [a, b], then there exists a number c in [a, b] such that f(c) = f_avg = (1/(b-a)) ∫_a^b f(x) dx, that is, ∫_a^b f(x) dx = f(c)(b - a).
natural.es: Si f es continua en [a, b], entonces existe un número c en [a, b] tal que f(c) = f_prom = (1/(b-a)) ∫_a^b f(x) dx, es decir, ∫_a^b f(x) dx = f(c)(b - a).

theorem.mean-value-theorem-integrals.notes: Stewart presents this as a consequence of the Intermediate Value Theorem applied to the integral function. It guarantees the existence of a point where the function attains its average value.

natural.en: Every bounded, monotonic sequence is convergent.
natural.es: Toda sucesión acotada y monótona es convergente.

theorem.monotonic-sequence-theorem.notes: Stewart states this theorem using the Completeness Axiom (least upper bound property). The proof relies on the existence of the supremum for bounded sets.

natural.en: The integral of a rate of change is the net change: ∫_a^b F'(x) dx = F(b) - F(a).
natural.es: La integral de una tasa de cambio es el cambio neto: ∫_a^b F'(x) dx = F(b) - F(a).

theorem.net-change-theorem.notes: This is a restatement of FTC Part 2 interpreted in terms of rates of change. Stewart presents it as a conceptual framework for applications (displacement, accumulated quantity, etc.).

natural.en: If n is any real number, then d/dx(x^n) = nx^{n-1}.
natural.es: Si n es cualquier número real, entonces d/dx(x^n) = nx^{n-1}.

theorem.power-rule.notes: Stewart proves the case n = positive integer using the binomial theorem in section 3.1. The general case (n any real number) is proved later using logarithmic differentiation in section 3.6.

natural.en: For a power series ∑ cₙ(x-a)ⁿ, there are only three possibilities: (i) The series converges only when x = a. (ii) The series converges for all x. (iii) There is a positive number R such that the series converges if |x-a| < R and diverges if |x-a| > R. R is called the radius of convergence.
natural.es: Para una serie de potencias ∑ cₙ(x-a)ⁿ, sólo se da una de tres posibilidades: (i) La serie converge sólo cuando x = a. (ii) La serie converge para todo x. (iii) Existe un número positivo R tal que la serie converge si |x-a| < R y diverge si |x-a| > R. R se llama radio de convergencia.

sources.author: James Stewart

natural.en: If the power series ∑ cₙ(x-a)ⁿ has radius of convergence R > 0, then the function f(x) = ∑_{n=0}^∞ cₙ(x-a)ⁿ is differentiable (and integrable) on (a-R, a+R) and (i) f'(x) = ∑_{n=1}^∞ n·cₙ(x-a)ⁿ⁻¹, (ii) ∫ f(x) dx = C + ∑_{n=0}^∞ cₙ(x-a)ⁿ⁺¹/(n+1). The radii of convergence of both series are R.
natural.es: Si la serie de potencias ∑ cₙ(x-a)ⁿ tiene radio de convergencia R > 0, entonces la función f(x) = ∑_{n=0}^∞ cₙ(x-a)ⁿ es diferenciable (e integrable) en (a-R, a+R) y (i) f'(x) = ∑_{n=1}^∞ n·cₙ(x-a)ⁿ⁻¹, (ii) ∫ f(x) dx = C + ∑_{n=0}^∞ cₙ(x-a)ⁿ⁺¹/(n+1). Los radios de convergencia de ambas series son R.

theorem.power-series-differentiation-int.notes: Stewart states this theorem and uses it extensively but defers the full proof to more advanced courses. The key result is that term-by-term differentiation and integration are valid within the interval of convergence.

natural.en: If f and g are both differentiable functions, then d/dx[f(x)g(x)] = f(x) g'(x) + g(x) f'(x).
natural.es: Si f y g son funciones diferenciables, entonces d/dx[f(x)g(x)] = f(x) g'(x) + g(x) f'(x).

theorem.product-rule.notes: Stewart proves this by adding and subtracting f(x+h)g(x) in the difference quotient.

natural.en: If f and g are differentiable functions, then d/dx[f(x)/g(x)] = [g(x)f'(x) - f(x)g'(x)] / [g(x)]^2.
natural.es: Si f y g son funciones diferenciables, entonces d/dx[f(x)/g(x)] = [g(x)f'(x) - f(x)g'(x)] / [g(x)]^2.

theorem.quotient-rule.notes: Stewart derives the quotient rule using a similar technique to the product rule, adding and subtracting f(x)g(x) in the numerator of the difference quotient.

natural.en: (i) If lim(n→∞) |aₙ₊₁/aₙ| = L < 1, then the series ∑ aₙ is absolutely convergent. (ii) If lim(n→∞) |aₙ₊₁/aₙ| = L > 1 or lim |aₙ₊₁/aₙ| = ∞, the series diverges. (iii) If L = 1, the test is inconclusive.
natural.es: (i) Si lim(n→∞) |aₙ₊₁/aₙ| = L < 1, entonces la serie ∑ aₙ es absolutamente convergente. (ii) Si lim(n→∞) |aₙ₊₁/aₙ| = L > 1 o lim |aₙ₊₁/aₙ| = ∞, la serie diverge. (iii) Si L = 1, la prueba no es concluyente.

natural.en: Let f be a function that satisfies the following three hypotheses: 1. f is continuous on the closed interval [a, b]. 2. f is differentiable on the open interval (a, b). 3. f(a) = f(b). Then there is a number c in (a, b) such that f'(c) = 0.
natural.es: Sea f una función que satisface las tres hipótesis siguientes: 1. f es continua en el intervalo cerrado [a, b]. 2. f es derivable en el intervalo abierto (a, b). 3. f(a) = f(b). Entonces existe un número c en (a, b) tal que f'(c) = 0.

theorem.rolles-theorem.notes: Stewart proves Rolle's theorem using the Extreme Value Theorem and Fermat's theorem. This serves as the key lemma for the Mean Value Theorem.

natural.en: (i) If lim(n→∞) ⁿ√|aₙ| = L < 1, then the series ∑ aₙ is absolutely convergent. (ii) If lim(n→∞) ⁿ√|aₙ| = L > 1 or lim ⁿ√|aₙ| = ∞, the series diverges. (iii) If L = 1, the test is inconclusive.
natural.es: (i) Si lim(n→∞) ⁿ√|aₙ| = L < 1, entonces la serie ∑ aₙ es absolutamente convergente. (ii) Si lim(n→∞) ⁿ√|aₙ| = L > 1 o lim ⁿ√|aₙ| = ∞, la serie diverge. (iii) Si L = 1, la prueba no es concluyente.

theorem.squeeze-theorem.latex: f(x) \leq g(x) \leq h(x) \;\text{ and }\; \lim_{x \to a} f(x) = \lim_{x \to a} h(x) = L \implies \lim_{x \to a} g(x) = L

natural.en: If f(x) ≤ g(x) ≤ h(x) when x is near a (except possibly at a) and lim(x→a) f(x) = lim(x→a) h(x) = L, then lim(x→a) g(x) = L.
natural.es: Si f(x) ≤ g(x) ≤ h(x) cuando x está cerca de a (excepto posiblemente en a) y lim(x→a) f(x) = lim(x→a) h(x) = L, entonces lim(x→a) g(x) = L.

theorem.squeeze-theorem.notes: Also known as the sandwich theorem or pinching theorem. Stewart uses it to prove lim(x→0) sin(x)/x = 1.

natural.en: If u = g(x) is a differentiable function whose range is an interval I and f is continuous on I, then ∫ f(g(x)) g'(x) dx = ∫ f(u) du.
natural.es: Si u = g(x) es una función derivable cuyo rango es un intervalo I y f es continua en I, entonces ∫ f(g(x)) g'(x) dx = ∫ f(u) du.

theorem.substitution-rule.notes: The substitution rule is the integration counterpart of the chain rule. It works by reversing the chain rule for derivatives.

natural.en: If g' is continuous on [a, b] and f is continuous on the range of u = g(x), then ∫_a^b f(g(x)) g'(x) dx = ∫_{g(a)}^{g(b)} f(u) du.
natural.es: Si g' es continua en [a, b] y f es continua en el rango de u = g(x), entonces ∫_a^b f(g(x)) g'(x) dx = ∫_{g(a)}^{g(b)} f(u) du.

natural.en: If f and g are differentiable functions, then d/dx[f(x) + g(x)] = d/dx f(x) + d/dx g(x).
natural.es: Si f y g son funciones diferenciables, entonces d/dx[f(x) + g(x)] = d/dx f(x) + d/dx g(x).

theorem.sum-rule.notes: Proved using the definition of the derivative and the sum law for limits.

natural.en: If f(x) = Tₙ(x) + Rₙ(x), where Tₙ is the nth-degree Taylor polynomial and Rₙ is the remainder, then if lim(n→∞) Rₙ(x) = 0 for |x-a| < R, we have f(x) = ∑_{n=0}^∞ f⁽ⁿ⁾(a)/n! · (x-a)ⁿ. By Taylor's inequality, if |f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(x)| ≤ M for |x-a| ≤ d, then |Rₙ(x)| ≤ M·dⁿ⁺¹/(n+1)!.
natural.es: Si f(x) = Tₙ(x) + Rₙ(x), donde Tₙ es el polinomio de Taylor de grado n y Rₙ es el residuo, entonces si lim(n→∞) Rₙ(x) = 0 para |x-a| < R, se tiene f(x) = ∑_{n=0}^∞ f⁽ⁿ⁾(a)/n! · (x-a)ⁿ. Por la desigualdad de Taylor, si |f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(x)| ≤ M para |x-a| ≤ d, entonces |Rₙ(x)| ≤ M·dⁿ⁺¹/(n+1)!.

theorem.taylor-convergence.notes: Taylor's inequality follows from the Lagrange form of the remainder in Taylor's theorem, which itself uses the MVT.
